title: Scaling Local Solvers with the Many-Body Expansion
authors: Federico Zahariev (Iowa State University, Ames Laboratory), Amr Sabry (Indiana University)
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30137v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce a Many-Body Expansion framework for scaling black-box solvers for discrete optimization. The method decomposes a large problem into fragments, repeatedly improves each fragment with the rest of the assignment held fixed, and then applies targeted corrections on unions of fragments. The solver itself is unchanged: it only receives a restricted subproblem and returns a candidate assignment. The framework separates decomposition from solver design. Moebius inversion gives an exact fragment expansion of the objective, and for pairwise objectives such as graph coloring, MAX-CUT, and QUBO the expansion closes at second order. The promoted solver is monotone by construction, terminates in finitely many productive sweeps for non-negative integer-valued objectives, and connects to junction-tree dynamic programming when the fragment interaction structure is acyclic and full response functions are propagated. On graph coloring benchmarks, the promoted versions of TabuSearch and simulated annealing (SA) generally outperform flat applications of the same solvers, often finding better solutions in less CPU time, and the gain proves insensitive to the choice of graph partition. A facility-location study delimits the claim: there the partition must respect the objective's interaction locality, and the promoted solver reaches within 0.3-1.4% of GLPK-certified optima at every tested size. The same wrapper interface is used in each solver-swap case, and the facility-location check reuses the same monotone guard with a sign-adjusted interaction diagnostic; the improvements therefore come from the MBE promotion mechanism rather than solver-specific tuning.

title: On the formal definition of average function for interval data
authors: Sergio F. Alonso, Susana Montes, Susana Diaz-Vazquez
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30138v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper addresses the formal definition of average functions for interval data, extending classical aggregation theory beyond precise numerical values to the more general setting of real-valued intervals. Recognizing that interval data nat- urally arise in contexts involving imprecision or uncertainty, we examine how established notions of averages and aggregation functions can be generalized when the underlying domain is no longer restricted to the unit interval, but instead encompasses the entire real line. We analyze the impact of different admissible orders on intervals, particularly focusing on the lattice order and several total orders, and provide rigorous definitions of idempotency and mono- tonicity in this context. Furthermore, we adapt and study classical families of aggregation operators such as power means, minimum, maximum, and median to the interval setting, characterizing when these operators satisfy the properties required of average functions for intervals. Our results highlight that the choice of order plays a crucial role in the behavior and suitability of these operators. This work lays a foundation for the systematic aggregation of interval-valued information, with potential applications in statistics, decision making, and fields where data imprecision is inherent.

title: A General Variable Neighborhood Search for Logistic Network Flow Design with Nonlinear Edge Costs and Transshipment Capacities
authors: Varvara Kovaleva, Alexander Ponomarenko
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30139v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the problem of routing multiple commodities through a logistic transport network so as to minimise the joint cost of vehicle movements and of transshipment (reload) operations at intermediate storages. The problem combines two features that are common in practice but rarely treated together: edge costs that are nonlinear in the transported volume, because freight is carried by vehicles of fixed capacity, and hard upper bounds on the volume that can be reloaded at each node. We formulate the problem as a mixed integer linear program in both an arc-based and a path-based form, derive its linear relaxation, and propose a metaheuristic solver based on General Variable Neighborhood Search (GVNS). The method works in the path space and relies on three problem-specific neighborhoods that generate new candidate paths by (i) shortest paths under a reload-aware metric, (ii) edges carrying partially loaded vehicles, and (iii) detours around congested storages. We evaluate the method on our open benchmark for this problem (arXiv:2606.20653): a corpus of realistic logistic networks calibrated on real road graphs of nine European countries, five U.S. states and the European part of Russia, with near-planar topology (Zipf city sizes, a spatial-network budget model, and a doubly constrained gravity demand model). On 35 synthetic and 15 real-geometry instances with up to 150 storages, GVNS returns solutions within about one percent of the best dual bound on small networks -- a branch-and-bound lower bound substantially tighter than the LP relaxation -- is stable across random seeds, and for a comparable wall-clock budget is up to 55% better than a time-limited exact solver on the medium instances.

title: The SMFCE Paradigm: A Unified Modeling Framework Based on State, Cost, and Extremal Evolution
authors: Wei Ba, Ang Fu, Shengsong Kong, Zhongchuan Fu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30140v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper proposes a unified modeling framework centered on "state-cost-extremal evolution," referred to as the SMFCE paradigm. The paradigm represents the effective state of a system as a point in a state space, characterizes state cost by a single-valued scalar field, and describes system evolution through local cost descent or local extremum selection. Its mathematical core employs classical tools from differential geometry, gradient systems, and dynamical systems. The contribution of this paper is not to reintroduce these foundational results, but to organize them into two operational modeling principles. On finite-dimensional smooth Riemannian manifolds under appropriate regularity conditions, the path independence of cost differences and the cost monotonicity of negative gradient flows follow directly from classical results, while the descent property of discrete local-minimum transitions follows directly from the definition of a minimum. For same-level iterative emergence and present-centeredness, the paper provides conditional mathematical formulations using, respectively, parameterized gradient systems and bifurcation theory, and Markov processes and receding-horizon optimization. The paper further introduces three layered metrics: cost quantity, directed coupling degree, and commitment fulfillment rate, at the state, transition, path, and system levels. Finally, the paper discusses semantic modeling of large language model training and inference within this framework, explicitly distinguishes classical mathematical results, conditional propositions, and empirical adaptation models, and provides reproducible empirical testing procedures for the two modeling principles.

title: Consensus-Aware Co-design of Wireless Multi-Agent Control and Communication Systems
authors: Atefeh Termehchi, Sajedeh Soleimani, Shiva Kazemi Taskooh, Mehdi Rasti, Ekram Hossain
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30141v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous multi-agent control systems (MACSs) enable distributed coordination in emerging applications such as smart power grids and autonomous vehicle or drone networks. In many of these applications, inter-agent communication relies on wireless networks. However, conventional MACS designs neglect the interaction between the communication and control subsystems. At the same time, conventional wireless designs reserve communication resources based on worst-case MACS requirements. Consequently, control performance is degraded and wireless resources are utilized inefficiently. To address these challenges, we propose a consensus-aware co-design approach for MACSs and wireless communication systems. We introduce a system model in which agents achieve consensus by exchanging information through device-to-device (D2D) links that share spectrum with cellular users under limited bandwidth resources. Based on this model, we formulate a joint optimization problem for consensus-topology selection and wireless resource allocation to minimize bandwidth consumption while guaranteeing consensus and satisfying the quality-of-service (QoS) requirements of both MACSs and cellular users. Although the resulting problem is a mixed-integer nonlinear program (NP-hard in general), a structural property of the optimal solution enables a sequential two-stage optimization algorithm with polynomial complexity. Simulations on a smart power grid case study demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves 24-27% bandwidth savings compared with the two baselines while maintaining consensus and satisfying all QoS requirements of the control agents and the communication users.

title: Strongly Regular Graph Construction via Quadratic Binary Optimization
authors: D. Osorio, P. Andagana, V. Gonz\'alez, J. Czartowski, D. Goyeneche
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30142v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Strongly regular graphs, hereafter SRGs, are highly structured combinatorial objects of central interest in algebraic graph theory and quantum information, whose explicit construction becomes rapidly intractable as the number of vertices grows; Conway's still unresolved $99$-graph problem is an emblematic example. The matrix equation defining SRGs is quadratic in the binary edge variables, so the natural penalty enforcing it, a sum of squared residuals, is quartic and lies outside quadratic unconstrained binary optimization, known as QUBO. We prove a considerably stronger obstruction, namely that no quadratic function of the edge variables has the labeled SRGs as its exact set of global minimizers, except for three degenerate families given by the perfect matchings, the cocktail-party graphs and the pentagon. In particular, we formally establish that the $99$-vertex graph of Conway's problem cannot be obtained from any QUBO over the edge variables without auxiliary variables. Guided by this theorem we develop two complementary algorithms. The first operates within pure QUBO, solves the degenerate families exactly, and beyond them works as a generate--prune--verify pipeline whose output is a reduced set of candidates certified by a polynomial-time classical test. The second solves the full problem by quadratizing this quartic penalty through Rosenberg auxiliary variables, whose number grows as $\Theta(N^3)$ with the number of vertices $N$. We test the pure-QUBO route under simulated annealing on all feasible families with at most $18$ vertices and the auxiliary-variable route on representative targets up to $16$ vertices, and tabulate the algebraically feasible parameter sets for graphs with at most $49$ vertices.

title: The Last Iterate of the Projected Stochastic Subgradient Method Pays a Logarithm, Even in Dimension One
authors: Guglielmo Beretta, Tommaso Cesari, Roberto Colomboni
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30143v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove that the projected stochastic subgradient method with the standard anytime stepsizes $\eta_t = \gamma/\sqrt t$ can suffer expected last-iterate optimization error of order $(\log n)/\sqrt n$ already on the real line. Combined with the classical in-expectation upper bound, this establishes the sharp worst-case order of the projected stochastic subgradient method.

title: Forward Tangent-Centered Sinkhorn DRO: Exact Nominal Recovery from Optimal Transport to KL
authors: Junjie Guo
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30144v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Fixed-reference entropy-regularized transport yields smooth distributionally robust optimization (DRO) objectives, but its value as a function of the adversarial marginal is generally minimized at a kernel-smoothed law rather than at the nominal distribution. Consequently, the smallest raw ambiguity set need not recover nominal risk. Building on prior information-geometric plan-KL orientations, we study the forward tangent-centered discrepancy obtained by subtracting the value and first variation at the nominal law. This is the unique affine recentering, up to the simplex gauge; for symmetric costs, its plan-KL representation coincides with the forward candidate noted by Amari et al. (2018). The representation shows that the discrepancy dominates marginal KL, is uniquely zero at the nominal law, and is strongly convex in total variation. The resulting DRO problem retains a scalar log-sum-exp dual and closed-form conditional adversarial weights. On finite supports with symmetric zero-diagonal costs, the discrepancy converges uniformly to the unregularized transport cost at low temperature; for any finite cost, its rescaled value converges uniformly to marginal KL at high temperature. We derive its exact local Hessian, an explicit finite-sample containment radius, and a generalized chi-square calibration for multinomial data. Controlled simulations verify nominal centering, both limiting regimes, and practical plug-in coverage.

title: Elimination Geometry II: Integrability, Representation, and Structural Limits
authors: Mian Huang, Xueqin Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30145v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Elimination geometry studies the exact nonnegative defect left after an auxiliary variable is optimized out. Part~II audits this certified-elimination interface through three theorem families.
  For integrability, local gaps form a repeated partial-elimination tower precisely under nonnegativity, touching, and zero elementary-square circulation. Hodge projection constructs nearest finite-space repairs and separates curvature, certification, and global period taxes. For representation and price, a descent gate characterizes surjective refinements and rules out strictly convex separable, duplication-invariant weight penalties. Dummy and target-calling lifts show that unrestricted lift design is vacuous, whereas the Fidelity-coherence frontier isolates irreducible cost. A modal Gram block classifies unconstrained quadratic lift-coupling germs and yields aligned Gaussian risk ledgers. Bernstein spectral functions preserve graph-Laplacian structure. Graph-universal Markov resolvents exist exactly up to first-order fractional qualification, and universal polynomial spectral penalties reduce to nonnegative Laplacian multiples. This linear limit does not preclude Part~I's nonlinear CDF repair and sharp CRPS theory.
  For converses, finite-order target-jet preservation uniquely requires subtraction of the corresponding defect jet, up to flat terms; approximate jets yield quasi-descent and stationary limits. Fixed-marginal coupling obeys a dependence-benefit frontier. Reversing certified KL in entropy-regularized control eliminates dimension-free guarantees, while a fixed measurement preserves all Umegaki defects of a faithful Gibbs family exactly when that family commutes.

title: A reciprocal graph-deviation functional: structural identifiability from controlled equilibrium maps
authors: Jonathan Washburn, Megan Simons
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30146v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We constructed a reciprocal graph-deviation functional for positive ratios on a finite weighted graph. Its scalar generator $J(x)=\tfrac12(x+x^{-1})-1$ was characterized previously by ratio-composition and unit log-curvature. Our principal new result was structural identifiability: already on a two-site, one-edge system, the complete minimizer-location map obtained by sweeping the boundary and site-to-edge weight ratio determines any reciprocal generator whose log-coordinate representation is $C^2$ with everywhere-positive curvature, up to a positive scale; unit-curvature calibration fixes that scale. For the calibrated reciprocal family~$J_p$ we obtained the equilibrium response in closed form. A synthetic $15$-condition sweep with seven simulated measurements per condition and log-scale noise $\sigma=0.05$ selected $J$ over~$J_{1.1}$ with probability~$0.997$ under exact boundary and weight parameters; a declared representation-uncertainty screen lowered that value to approximately~$0.88$. These probabilities characterize the simulated design under the declared data-generating model. The finite sweep discriminated prespecified generators, whereas nonparametric recovery required the complete response map. We also recorded the associated convex gradient-flow and Langevin dynamics.

title: Sufficient Conditions for Exact Convergence Time in Prescribed-Time Control
authors: Jiyuan Kuang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30147v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we propose a series of theoretical results for prescribed-time control to rigorously prove that the closed-loop system will not reach the equilibrium point before the prescribed time. Thus, it is convenient to prove that the settling time is exactly equal to the prescribed time instant. In other words, conservative estimation of the settling time, which often accompanies classical finite-/fixed-time or prescribed-time control results, is theoretically avoided in this paper. Specifically, we introduce a local Lipschitz condition, a local homogeneous linear-growth condition, and an Osgood condition in sequence. Both reduction to absurdity and the Lyapunov method are applied to demonstrate that the system cannot converge to zero before the prescribed time instant. Finally, the proposed framework is applied to prescribed-time controllers based on adaptive backstepping, parametric Lyapunov equations, and distributed leader-following consensus, demonstrating the generality of the proposed results.

title: Do Machine Learning-Guided Proactive Full Capacity Protocols Mitigate Emergency Department Overcrowding? A Simulation-Based Evaluation
authors: Khalid Aram, Orhun Vural, Bunyamin Ozaydin, James Booth, Abdulaziz Ahmed
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30148v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Objective: Emergency department (ED) overcrowding threatens care quality, yet Full Capacity Protocols (FCPs) are typically activated only after crowding thresholds have been exceeded. This study evaluated whether machine learning-guided proactive FCP activation improves ED crowding control compared with conventional reactive activation.
  Materials and Methods: We developed and validated an integrated machine learning and discrete-event simulation framework representing ED patient flow and capacity management. An embedded machine learning model predicted hourly waiting-room crowding six hours ahead and triggered proactive FCP activation. Using empirically calibrated operational parameters from a large US hospital, we compared proactive and reactive deployment strategies over a 365-day simulation horizon with 10 independent replications. Outcomes included ED length of stay, wait time, percentage of time above the crowding threshold, number of FCP activations, and protocol duration.
  Results: Proactive deployment produced statistically significant reductions in the percentage of time above the crowding threshold and average protocol duration across all threshold settings. It also reduced crowding variability and extreme congestion events, resulting in smoother ED operations. Although proactive deployment generally improved ED length of stay and wait time, these differences were not statistically significant.
  Conclusion: Embedding machine learning predictions within an operational simulation enables proactive, prediction-guided capacity management before severe congestion develops. These findings support the feasibility and potential value of proactive FCP deployment as a decision-support strategy for improving ED crowding control and provide evidence to support prospective implementation in clinical practice.

title: A Tutte-Like Theorem for Injective Flows on Meshes
authors: Darsh Kaushik, Noam Aigerman
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30149v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This work proves a theorem regarding injectivity of continuous flows that are defined via discrete vector fields on triangle meshes. In similar fashion to Tutte's embedding, the theorem shows a connection between harmonicity and injectivity. Specifically, a discrete harmonic function is computed over a spherical mesh, and its $90^\circ$-rotated gradients are taken as the vector field. We show that this leads to an injective flow over the mesh, i.e., when two points are advected along the vector field, their trajectories are guaranteed to not intersect. The core insight behind this theorem is that the characterization of the Poincar\'e-Hopf indices of discrete harmonic 1-forms is paralleled in the combinatorial rules for injective vector fields. Similarly to Tutte's embedding, the injective vector field can be computed by simply solving a sparse linear system. Furthermore, it is differentiably dependent on the entries of the Laplacian, enabling unconstrained gradient-based optimization of the vector field while preserving injectivity. The advection itself can be computed by a quick and accurate algorithm. We experimentally validate the injectivity of the results, as well as show examples of differentiable optimization, such as computing an injective approximation to a given non-injective vector field, and fitting an injective vector field to satisfy constraints.

title: The Gittins Index for a Transparent One-Armed Bandit with a Continuous Payoff Spectrum in Equilibrium States
authors: Marcin Makowski, Edward W. Piotrowski, Jan L. Cie\'sli\'nski
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30150v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present an analogue of the classical Gittins index for a one-armed decision problem with a continuous spectrum of payoffs. The model assumes that the decision-maker observes independent realizations of a random variable and, at each step, decides whether to accept the current opportunity or continue observing. We show that the optimal strategy takes the form of a threshold rule, while the corresponding reservation index is determined by a one-dimensional fixed-point equation with a direct decision-theoretic interpretation. The model is illustrated with an example of bookmaker betting related to horse racing and the Kelly criterion. This perspective allows the proposed index to be viewed as a threshold of informational advantage. This, in turn, points to potential applications in optimal stopping problems and decision-making under uncertainty.

title: Advance versus Spot Selling in Queueing Systems: the Effect of Uncertainty Sources
authors: Yumeng Liu, Dongyuan Zhan
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30156v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop an unobservable M/M/1 queueing model to analyze advance selling and spot selling under uncertainty. Customers are heterogeneous in waiting costs, drawn from a uniform distribution. We disentangle two fundamental sources of uncertainty: customer valuation and service capacity. We derive the respective revenue functions for both advance and spot selling strategies and compare their performance. Our analysis reveals that advance selling is more profitable when customer valuations are uncertain. Conversely, spot selling emerges as the more profitable strategy when uncertainty originates from service capacity. When both sources are present, our numerical experiments suggest that the preferred regime depends on the relative dispersion of the two uncertainties: advance selling tends to be favored when valuation uncertainty is sufficiently pronounced relative to capacity uncertainty, whereas spot selling tends to be favored when capacity uncertainty is more pronounced. These results highlight how the origin and magnitude of uncertainty shape the optimal selling strategy in service queues and offer practical guidance for platforms and service providers deciding between advance and spot selling.

title: Smooth maps onto regions in Euclidean spaces respecting height functions
authors: Naoki Kitazawa
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30163v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: One of interest of the author lies in the canonical projections of the unit spheres and generalizations. He is interested in the canonical projections of embedded manifolds in the higher dimensional Euclidean spaces, including height functions, especially, their construction and representations by explicit equations. This is a kind of fundamental studies on construction or global theory on singularity theory of differentiable maps, closely related to differential geometry, differential topology, and algebraic geometry. Rather than knowing existence, construction has been difficult in certain senses.
  We construct smooth maps onto regions in Euclidean spaces locally modeled by height functions and show new examples. This is related to a pioneering study of the author, certain generalizations of the canonical projections of the unit spheres (, so-called special generic maps), and construction of them as projections of connected components of the zero sets of some smooth maps to some Euclidean spaces.

title: Triple Products of Correlated Multivariate Hermite Polynomials
authors: Laura Lyman
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30204v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Stochastic Galerkin schemes (SGS) are used to approximate solutions to differential equations with stochastic parameters. In particular, they express the solution with an infinite orthogonal functional basis of the parameter space and derive a deterministic system of PDEs; the solution of this deterministic system can be used to produce a {surrogate} approximation of the original stochastic equations. When the parameters are correlated, the infinite series representation of the solution does not provably converge for all joint distributions; further, classic decorrelating transformations (e.g., Roseblatt) often introduce known numerical instabilities. Rahman (2017) established convergence in probability and distribution for correlated {Gaussian} parameters when the basis functionals are {multivariate Hermite polynomials} (MHPs), where these polynomials are only {weakly orthogonal} with respect to the underlying joint density. Due to weak orthogonality, the $N$th moments of MHPs introduced during Galerkin projection do not trivially decompose into products of one-dimensional expectations and have no closed-form expression for $N > 2$; consequently, these moments are typically estimated via brute-force sampling and quickly become prohibitively expensive to compute. In this paper, we introduce and prove several foundational results for MHPs. These results culminate in an equation that can be used to calculate the $N = 3$ moments (triple products) exactly, whose implementation dramatically reduces the computational bottleneck otherwise inherent to SGS with correlated Gaussian parameters.

title: Higher-order tangent and secant numbers, special-value integrals, and a common zero attractor
authors: Luc Rams\`es Talla Waffo
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30208v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study two families of coefficients associated with powers of the tangent function and with products of the secant and tangent functions, and develop a unified treatment of the corresponding higher-order tangent and secant numbers. The first part establishes a common identity for even derivatives of $\tanh x$ and odd derivatives of $\operatorname{sech}x$. Combined with integral formulae for these derivatives, this yields finite power-integral representations for the normalized values $\zeta(2n+1)$ and $\beta(2n)$ and naturally introduces two polynomial families $P_n$ and $Q_n$.
  We determine several arithmetic and structural properties of these polynomials. In particular, we identify the exact content of $P_n$, prove that $Q_n$ is primitive, establish strict log-concavity and unimodality of their coefficient sequences, and describe their real zeros. For even indices each family has a unique negative real zero, and the two sequences of real zeros have the same limit. We also derive differential recurrences and generating functions for $P_n$ and $Q_n$.
  The generating functions lead to a global complex-singularity analysis. We construct a compact Jordan curve $\Gamma$ and prove that the complex zero sets of both $P_n$ and $Q_n$ converge to $\Gamma$ in Hausdorff distance. The normalized zero-counting measures converge weakly to the same equilibrium measure on $\Gamma$. We determine the logarithmic capacity of the enclosed compact set, give an explicit arclength density for the limiting measure, and compute its first moments. Numerical plots for $P_{20}$, $P_{50}$, $P_{100}$ and $P_{150}$ illustrate the zero-attractor theorem.

title: Finite zero products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols
authors: Youqi Liu, Jie Qin, Sui Huang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30209v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study finite products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Fock space over the complex plane. If every symbol has the form $f+\overline g$, where $f$ and $g$ are entire functions of exponential type, we prove that a finite product vanishes if and only if one symbol vanishes identically. It suffices to test the product on reproducing kernels. The proof represents the product by a two-variable entire function and transforms the equation for a left factor by $\exp(-\partial_z\partial_w)$. A Fock norm identity then permits cancellation of each nonzero factor.

title: Relaxation and $\Gamma$-Convergence of Stretch Energy on Surface Homeomorphisms
authors: Shu-Yung Liu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30214v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Area-preserving parameterization of triangular meshes is an essential task in geometry processing, yet an exactly area-preserving simplicial mapping may not exist in general. In this paper, we study area preservation of simplicial mappings in the limit of mesh refinement by establishing the $\Gamma$-convergence of the discrete stretch energy, a functional that measures their area distortion. We first introduce its limit functional, the relaxed stretch energy on surface homeomorphisms, defined through the pushforward of the area measure, and show that it is the relaxation of the stretch energy of diffeomorphisms with respect to uniform convergence. Then, to compare simplicial mappings with homeomorphisms, we construct a geometric lift that requires no shape-regularity assumption on the image mesh. Finally, we establish the $\Gamma$-convergence and show that the minimal discrete energies converge to the continuum minimum. Moreover, any homeomorphism arising as a limit of lifted discrete local minimizers in fixed-radius balls is area-preserving.

title: Ergodic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control with Stochastic Coefficients
authors: Xuyang Lin, Nizar Touzi
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30219v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We investigate ergodic linear-quadratic optimal control problems with stochastic coefficients and introduce the associated stochastic ergodic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, in which the classical ergodic constant is replaced by a random process $\lambda$. We establish well-posedness of the equation and show that $\lambda$ characterizes the optimal ergodic costs for a general class of averaging kernels, including those corresponding to normalized finite-horizon and discounted costs. For random-periodic coefficients, we construct a random-periodic solution and show that the optimal ergodic costs associated with all admissible averaging kernels coincide. We also establish stability of the optimal ergodic costs under perturbations of the coefficients.

title: DBDSVDMR3: An MRRR-Based Bidiagonal SVD Solver Built from DSTEGR
authors: James Demmel, Inderjit Dhillon, Sai Surya Duvvuri, Julien Langou, Osni Marques, Ryan Schneider
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30227v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The optimal algorithm for the symmetric tridiagonal eigenvalue problem is Multiple Relatively Robust Representations (MRRR or MR$^3$), which is capable of computing $k$ eigenvalue/eigenvector pairs in only $O(kn)$ floating-point operations. While MRRR is nearly 30 years old, it has never successfully been adapted to the bidiagonal SVD. This is not for lack of trying; two previous attempts produced implementations that were considered for LAPACK but eventually abandoned, a result of the fact that neither was reliable enough when run on test problems. The question therefore remained: is there a problem with the theory of MRRR for the bidiagonal SVD or were there simply bugs in the previous implementations that went undetected? This paper resolves this question by presenting DBDSVDMR3 -- a new implementation of the MRRR-based algorithm for the bidiagonal SVD originally proposed by Willems and Lang [ETNA 2012], which, for the first time, performs well on a variety of test problems while achieving significant speedups over both LAPACK's bisection-based solver and, in certain cases, divide-and-conquer for the bidiagonal SVD (thereby indicating that the theory is sound). DBDSVDMR3 will be available in the next release of LAPACK. In this paper, we discuss the design of our implementation, which was obtained with the help of Claude Code, and exhibit its performance on a diverse set of test problems.

title: Summation-by-parts operators for general function spaces: Flux differencing, entropy stability, and accuracy
authors: Henry M. Haase, Andrew R. Winters, Jan Glaubitz
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30272v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Summation-by-parts (SBP) operators are a cornerstone of provably stable high-order methods for hyperbolic conservation laws. For nonlinear problems, the flux-differencing framework of Fisher and Carpenter combines such SBP operators with entropy-conservative two-point fluxes to obtain semi-discretizations that are conservative in the sense of Lax--Wendroff and discretely entropy-conservative or stable. So far, this framework has been developed exclusively for operators that are exact for polynomials. Function-space SBP (FSBP) operators lift this restriction by being exact on a general finite-dimensional function space that can be tailored to the problem at hand. In this work, we extend flux differencing to FSBP operators for general (potentially non-polynomial) function spaces. We prove that, whenever the operator has a diagonal norm and its function space contains the constants, the resulting semi-discretization is conservative in the sense of Lax--Wendroff, semi-discretely entropy-conservative within a single element, and entropy-stable across element interfaces. We also provide the first theoretical accuracy analysis of FSBP operators: We characterize their design order through an algebraic criterion on the underlying function space, prove that suitable non-polynomial spaces achieve the same design order as polynomial spaces of equal dimension, and show that the flux-differencing semi-discretization retains this order. Notably, the entropy-conservative two-point flux is reused unchanged; only the underlying function space differs from the polynomial case. Numerical experiments for the Burgers' equation and the compressible Euler equations in one and two dimensions confirm these properties.

title: Continuous-time analysis and algorithms for linear and convex quadratic programs via exactly solvable differential inclusions
authors: Gabriel P. Langlois, Akwum Onwunta, J\'er\^ome Darbon
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30300v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Linear and convex quadratic programs are fundamental problems in optimization. While many methods have been developed for solving these programs in large-scale applications, to our knowledge none have attempted to solve their continuous-time gradient flow, a differential inclusion, in full generality without assumptions beyond feasibility. Recent work solved the gradient flows in two special cases, basis pursuit and the lasso, and obtained competitive algorithms. Motivated by these results, we solve the general case exactly. Using the minimal selection principle for monotone differential inclusions, we show that the trajectory of the gradient flow consists of finitely many pieces, each obtained from one nonnegative least-squares problem. Its final piece yields an optimal solution or a certificate of unboundedness. This analysis leads to two algorithms. The first algorithm is exact, terminates after finitely many steps, and applies to linear programs and projections onto polyhedra. The second algorithm, which we call minimal selection descent, discretizes the gradient flow for general convex quadratic programs. Its iterates converge to an optimal solution when one exists and otherwise certify unboundedness. We apply both algorithms to a positivity-preserving limiter for a discontinuous Galerkin scheme and to optimal control problems for the Poisson and heat equations. In the limiter, the first algorithm conserves the total mass more accurately than the state-of-the-art Douglas--Rachford splitting method. On the control problems, minimal selection descent reaches the optimal value to machine precision and is competitive in time with commercial and open-source solvers.

title: Structure-Preserving Dimension Reduction and Surrogates for Partially Linear Bayesian Inverse Problems
authors: Ziheng Zhang, Dingcheng Luo, Thomas O'Leary-Roseberry, Umberto Villa, Omar Ghattas
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30306v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many Bayesian inverse problems are characterized by two parameter vectors with distinct roles. A medium property, operator coefficient, or geometry block enters the forward model nonlinearly, whereas a volumetric, initial condition, or boundary condition source enters linearly. General-purpose nonlinear surrogates must relearn this known source dependence from data and may not preserve the correct source scaling outside the training regime. We introduce a structure-preserving partially linear (SPPL) framework that constructs separate reduced spaces for outputs, (linearly appearing) sources, and (nonlinearly appearing) medium variables and represents the reduced forward map as an affine function of the retained source coordinates, with coefficients that depend on the medium variables. Here, "affine" refers to the retained, mean-centered source coordinates: the physical forward map remains linear in the source, while the affine offset is induced by the source-prior mean and vanishes when that mean is zero. The analysis first identifies the optimal blockwise ridge approximation and then derives the optimal affine-in-source approximation under independent medium and source priors. A direct decomposition of the forward error into output, source, medium, and surrogate contributions yields blockwise spectral criteria and prior-predictive expected-KL control. For a Gaussian source prior, the optimal affine-in-source approximation coincides with the optimal blockwise ridge approximation. In a coseismic numerical example, a three-model controlled ablation on common block-reduced coordinates separates the effects of coefficient-matrix supervision and structure-preserving affine-in-source parameterization. Reduced-space surrogate MCMC provides orders-of-magnitude online acceleration relative to high-fidelity posterior sampling.

title: Matrix-Free Local Multigrid for $C^1$ Hermite Discretizations on GPUs
authors: Micha{\l} Wichrowski
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30308v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: I present a matrix-free local multigrid method for $C^1$ tensor-product Hermite discretizations on adaptively refined Cartesian meshes, using the clamped biharmonic problem as the model problem. Extending a cell-wise primal-dual formulation to Hermite elements, I enforce continuity through a constraint operator that is never formed. At refinement edges, geometric prolongation supplies both the trace and its normal derivative, so the local V-cycle needs no edge operator and no hanging-node machinery. For the cubic element, an even-odd decomposition based on the signed reflection symmetry of the Hermite basis, applied along two axes, splits the element matrix into four dense $16\times16$ blocks and reaches 85% of peak memory bandwidth. Chebyshev-Jacobi and vertex-patch smoothers both preserve conformity by construction. In three dimensions on one NVIDIA A100 in double precision, conjugate gradients preconditioned by the Chebyshev-Jacobi V-cycle need five or six iterations on uniform meshes and solve at up to 4.23 million cells per second. On locally refined meshes the count rises to at most sixteen, ordered by the fraction of cells on a refinement edge and nearly equal for both smoothers.

title: On the Adversarial Vulnerability of Neural Receivers with Unrolled LDPC Decoders
authors: Aakash Saini, Jafar Aco Mohammadi, Wolfgang Gerstacker
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30345v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Neural receivers for 5G New Radio (NR) match classical model-based receivers in link-level performance, but their robustness to adversarial perturbations at the receiver input remains underexplored. We show that standard gradient-based attacks applied end-to-end through an unrolled low-density parity-check (LDPC) decoder fail to significantly outperform a matched-power Gaussian perturbation. We identify the failure as gradient masking caused by tanh saturation in the boxplus operation of the belief-propagation (BP) check-node update, with a per-iteration gradient norm decay of more than four orders of magnitude across ten unrolled BP iterations. Based on this finding, we propose two structurally independent loss functions that restore attack efficacy. L_BP routes the gradient through the unsaturated early iterations via per-iteration supervision, while L_LLR is a margin loss on pre-decoder log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) whose gradient bypasses the LDPC decoder entirely. Both loss functions increase the block-error rate (BLER) by one to four orders of magnitude at matched perturbation power, with the results reproduced on both the Sionna NeuralReceiver and DeepRx. At low PSR, L_LLR-optimized perturbations achieve up to three orders of magnitude higher BLER on unseen channel realizations than LBP-optimized perturbations.

title: Partial Breakdown of Integrability in Nearly Integrable Systems
authors: Marian Gidea, Shoya Motonaga
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30354v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the persistence of integrable structures in real-analytic nearly integrable systems under perturbations that may destroy some, but not all, of these structures. Specifically, we establish upper bounds on the numbers of real-analytic first integrals -- quantities conserved by the motion -- and commuting vector fields -- infinitesimal generators of continuous symmetries -- that can persist under the perturbation. These bounds are expressed in terms of Melnikov-type functions, which quantify the breakdown of the corresponding integrable structures. Unlike classical Melnikov theory, our conditions occur even in the absence of zeros of the Melnikov functions, so they do not necessarily imply the existence of homoclinic tangles. We give a geometric interpretation of these conditions in the context of the Arnold diffusion problem, showing that they imply micro-diffusion. We also obtain a criterion for higher-dimensional nearly integrable systems in which the dimension of the span of the Melnikov vectors restricts the numbers of possible first integrals and commuting vector fields. This shows that the geometry of the Melnikov vectors provides a new mechanism for detecting the breakdown of integrability. We give several applications to integrable Hamiltonian systems subject to forcing and dissipation.

title: A unified variational framework for augmented Lagrangian preconditioning of saddle point systems: applications to mixed-dimensional and fictitious domain methods
authors: Michele Benzi, Marco Feder, Luca Heltai, Federica Mugnaioni
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30357v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a general framework to derive augmented Lagrangian preconditioners for saddle point systems arising from mixed finite element discretizations. Our approach is based on augmenting the variational formulation at the continuous level prior to discretization, providing a unified strategy for designing efficient preconditioners that are robust under mesh refinement for a broad class of problems leading to symmetric saddle point systems. The robustness of the proposed preconditioners is established through a detailed spectral analysis. This framework is applied to different model problems, focusing on mixed-dimensional and fictitious domain formulations involving Lagrange multipliers, with some configurations featuring large coefficient jumps. Extensive numerical experiments on different test cases and geometries are presented, validating the effectiveness and robustness of our preconditioners when used in conjunction with flexible GMRES.

title: A Transformer-based Approach for Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning with Varying Initial/Final Conditions
authors: Qian Zhang, Shanqing Liu, Jerome Darbon, George Karniadakis
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30388v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We address the problem of real-time multi-agent path planning under prescribed initial and final configurations, formulated as a high-dimensional optimal control problem subject to inter-agent collision avoidance and obstacle constraints. Classical solvers based on the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation or Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) become computationally intractable as the number of agents grows, due to the curse of dimensionality and the non-convexity introduced by interaction constraints. We propose OCFormer, a transformer-based neural network that parameterizes the inverse of a coordinate transformation mapping a simple, analytically tractable latent space, in which agents evolve independently under a decoupled Hamiltonian, to the physical space of the coupled, interacting system. The model is trained by minimizing a physics-informed loss comprising the Hamiltonian ODE residual from the PMP and a boundary matching term, without requiring pre-computed trajectory data. The self-attention mechanism endows OCFormer with permutation equivariance over agents, a structural symmetry that prior symplectic network approaches do not natively enforce. When trained on a distribution of boundary conditions, the amortized OCFormer produces near-optimal trajectories for unseen initial and final configurations in a single forward pass ($\sim$220ms), enabling real-time inference without retraining. We further introduce a lightweight transfer learning framework that adapts a pretrained OCFormer to out-of-distribution perturbations in seconds via L-BFGS fine-tuning. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional multi-agent navigation with up to 128 agents demonstrate the scalability and efficiency of the proposed approach.

title: Robust topology optimization of isogeometric Kirchhoff--Love shells by the Speed Method
authors: Philipp Eisenhardt, Fernando H\"ubner Scherer, Barbara Wohlmuth, Andrei Constantinescu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30389v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper presents a framework for robust topology optimization of Kirchhoff-Love (KL) multi-patch shells using isogeometric analysis and non-matching meshes and provides a CAD-compatible method. The material distribution is optimized via a NURBS-based level set method, enabling accurate boundary representation and seamless export to standard CAD/CAM workflows. The shape derivative is computed using the speed method, yielding a volume-based formulation that avoids boundary approximations and aligns with the isogeometric principle of coarse, high-order discretizations. This eliminates the need for local refinement, adaptive quadrature, or trimming as the descent direction for the compliance and volume objectives are obtained through a biharmonic equation. The framework is extended to robust optimization under uncertainty, accounting for stochastic loading and material properties via Monte Carlo sampling and Gaussian Random Fields. Numerical examples demonstrate the method's efficiency and robustness across single- and multi-patch shells, reproducing literature results with fewer elements than traditional FEM or refined IGA approaches. The developed methods and tools can be directly extended to problems involving stress-based optimization and risk-averse metrics. The numerical implementations are open-source and available on GitHub.

title: Outage Analysis and Bilevel Resource Optimization in RIS-Assisted Clustered UAV-NOMA Networks
authors: Masoud Ghazikor, Ly V. Nguyen, Morteza Hashemi
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30410v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper investigates RIS-assisted downlink UAV communications based on NOMA. Since conventional NOMA becomes difficult to scale as the number of UAVs grows, we develop a cluster-based UAV-NOMA framework in which a BS serves multiple UAV groups with the aid of partitionable RISs. Within this framework, we consider direct, RIS-only indirect, and composite links, and develop an analytical model for the received SNR and outage performance under Nakagami-$m$ and double Nakagami-$m$ fading with imperfect SIC. To enable scalable transmission, we introduce a greedy RIS-aware (GRIS) clustering method, which groups UAVs according to spatial and channel-related features. Based on the resulting clusters and RIS assignment, we formulate an efficiency-reliability bilevel optimization problem that jointly optimizes inter-cluster BS power allocation, intra-cluster NOMA power coefficients, and RIS element assignment. Specifically, the outer efficiency problem maximizes the average throughput across clusters, while the inner reliability problem minimizes the worst-UAV outage probability within each cluster. To solve the formulated problem, we propose a two-level iterative framework consisting of an inter-cluster outer-efficiency solver (IOS) and an intra-cluster inner-reliability solver (I2S), where I2S combines a grid-based progressive search (GPS) for NOMA power refinement with reliability-guided RIS element reassignment, and IOS updates the BS power weights. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of GRIS clustering, while pre-optimization analysis reveals efficiency-reliability trade-offs in power allocation. Baseline comparisons illustrate the ability of IOS-I2S to balance efficiency and reliability, while ablation studies highlight the importance of joint optimization.

title: New criteria for upper bounds on the number of limit cycles in Li\'enard systems
authors: Chen Cao, Hebai Chen, Yilei Tang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30417v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study upper bounds for isolated periodic orbits of generalized Li\'enard systems on a single potential well. Common-curvature and common-intercept conditions yield uniqueness and hyperbolicity, while a convex--concave condition on the potential-profile slopes gives an upper bound of two. The statements allow finite unequal potential endpoints; appropriate versions also admit degenerate restoring forces and reduced regularity. We prove a uniqueness extension across slope interfaces, a quantitative joint weak-damping criterion, and a compensation criterion controlled by two derivatives. A separate response comparison at neutral cycles, combined with a connected parameter-family argument, gives a coefficient criterion for a two-cycle bound. Applications include classical quartic systems, negative-parameter and positive-parameter Selkov systems, a uniqueness conjecture for arbitrary-degree polynomial systems, and explicit smooth and nonsmooth examples. Existence is proved separately whenever an exact count is asserted. Restrictions to a potential well, a parameter region, or a compact width interval are retained throughout.

title: Energy-rate equidistribution for adaptive SSAV--BDF2 integration of gradient flows
authors: Suki Shergill, JF Williams
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30454v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop an adaptive time-stepping strategy for scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) schemes combined with variable-step BDF2 discretization for gradient flows. The strategy selects step sizes based on the instantaneous energy dissipation rate and enforces monotonicity of a computable symmetric energy through a step rejection mechanism.
  We show that the step-size rules used in practice correspond to equidistributing a monitor function along the energy curve, connecting energy-adaptive time stepping to the classical theory of r-adaptive mesh methods. The monitor $g = |\dot{E}|$ is asymptotically optimal as it minimises the leading-order maximum symmetric-energy discrepancy for a given number of steps. A combined monitor that switches to $g = \sqrt{|\dot{E}|}$ near equilibrium caps step growth without degrading this error bound. The arclength parameter $\beta$ used in prior work is shown to be the ratio of the largest permitted step to the energy-error tolerance.
  The controller is paired with the SSAV--BDF2 discretization. Accepted steps satisfy monotonicity of the symmetric energy, from which we deduce a bound on the physical energy that is uniform in the number of steps, $\sup_n E(u^n) \le E(u^{0}) + \tau_1 + O(\Delta t_{\max}^2)$, and the scheme achieves second-order global accuracy under standard step-ratio restrictions. Numerical experiments on Cahn--Hilliard, Ohta--Kawasaki, Phase--Field Crystal, and functionalized Cahn--Hilliard models confirm the theory and demonstrate the method's efficiency.

title: Fefferman--Chang-type atomic decompositions for product Hardy spaces associated with Schr\"odinger operators
authors: Agnieszka Hejna-{\L}y\.zwa
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30459v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We establish a geometric (Fefferman--Chang-type) atomic characterization of the two-parameter Hardy space associated with a pair of Schr\"odinger operators $L_i=-\Delta+V_i$ on $\mathbb R^{n_i}$, $i=1,2$. The space is defined by the product conical square function. We assume comparability of neighbouring covering cubes, a local bound on the potentials, and decay of the semigroup mass at large scales.
  We prove that the Hardy norm is equivalent to a sum of classical local product Hardy norms at scales determined by the adapted coverings. This localization formula yields an atomic decomposition whose atoms satisfy size and partial cancellation conditions, with cancellation required only below the corresponding local scales. Both the atoms and their rectangular components remain supported inside fixed enlargements of the covering rectangles.
  The proof combines one-parameter Schr\"odinger Hardy space characterizations with standard vector-valued arguments and a localized product atomic decomposition with uniform control of scales and supports. The assumptions cover the model case of reverse H\"older potentials $V\in RH_q$, $q>n/2$, as well as potentials outside every $RH_q$ class, $q>1$, including half-space indicators and exponential potentials.

title: A smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres with Bernoulli geodesic flow
authors: Keith Burns, Tomas Gedeon, Yuping Ruan
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30464v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We construct a smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres whose geodesic flow is Bernoulli with respect to the Liouville measure.

title: Comb Tensor Network Finite-Difference Time-Domain Algorithms for 2D and 3D Electromagnetic Simulations
authors: Jonathan Tabares, Erika Ye, Yang Liu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30486v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper presents efficient 2D and 3D finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithms augmented by the comb tensor network (CTN) representation of the field and auxiliary quantities. The proposed CTN-FDTD algorithm leverages superior compressibility of CTN compared with quantized tensor train (QTT), and rank-reduction strategies including local and global smoothing techniques to achieve logarithmic memory requirement and computation (per time step) cost. Numerical examples validate these complexities and demonstrate the applicability of CTN-FDTD using a variety of source excitation, frequency and permittivity profiles in both 2D and 3D. Remarkably, CTN-FDTD can simulate 35 trillion spatial grid points in 3D with low memory and computation costs on one computation node, whereas standard FDTD would require 281 TB memory to store each of its 31 3D arrays. Moreover, CTN-FDTD was applied to realistic 2D photonic crystal structure simulation with one million grid points and 3D scattering analysis with 8.6 billion grid points.

title: Discovery of Singularities in Partial Differential Equations Using Adaptive Numerical Discretizations
authors: Allen Yang, Lucas Amoudruz, Petros Koumoutsakos
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30492v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We compute self-similar singularity profiles of partial differential equations (PDEs) using adaptive numerical discretizations based on optimizing a discrete loss (ODIL). The fields are represented in overlapping local Chebyshev patches joined with a mapped asymptotic patch. After factoring out the leading power laws of solution ansatzes, their limiting amplitudes at infinity are determined by the optimization, eliminating domain truncation and prescribed far-field conditions. Adaptive refinement is guided by Chebyshev-coefficient decay, and the nonlinear least-squares problem is solved using automatically differentiated Gauss--Newton iterations with Levenberg--Marquardt damping. The method achieves O(10^{-14})-level accuracy for Burgers profiles, residuals of O(10^{-14}) to O(10^{-10}) for the generalized De Gregorio family, and of O(10^{-8}) in a local region for the two-dimensional Boussinesq equations. These results demonstrate that ODIL can identify singularity profiles for PDEs with high accuracy using adaptive numerical methods, complementing ongoing efforts that rely on artificial intelligence.

title: Entropy bounded compact stencil Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin method for hyperbolic conservation laws
authors: Deepak Kumar, Pratima Rai, Arvind Patel
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30496v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper we introduce a compact stencil Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin method for the Euler equations of compressible gas dynamics, which preserves a minimum entropy principle similar to that introduced by Tadmor for entropy solution of the Euler equations [4]. Compact stencil RKDG, introduced by Chen et al. in [15], is a variant of standard RKDG method which is known for its smaller stencil size and parallel efficiency. The main challenge is that the cRKDG method has to be expressed in Butcher form and not every Runge-Kutta method of this form is a convex combination of forward-Euler steps. Therefore, in order to establish this property we leverage the bound preserving framework of the cRKDG schemes [8], an entropy bounded limiter [6] and the classical positivity preserving limiter. In the last section numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the robustness of the method.

title: An F-Type Normal-Reference Calibration for High-Dimensional Covariance Testing
authors: Pengfei Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30497v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An F-type normal-reference calibration is developed for testing equality of two high-dimensional covariance matrices with unknown means. The test statistic is a ratio whose numerator measures the Frobenius covariance discrepancy and whose denominator estimates its null expectation. Their difference is the complete Li-Chen statistic. Under suitable moment and trace conditions, we establish a Gaussian-reference approximation. After standardization, the statistic and its reference share the normal or nonnormal limits determined by a convergent normalized spectrum. The reference is a ratio of independent chi-square-type mixtures. Applying Welch-Satterthwaite matching to its two components gives an ordinary F approximation, with degrees of freedom estimated from independent four-observation blocks. The effect of estimating the population means is controlled by an exact expansion, and local-power and consistency results are established. The ordinary F approximation is asymptotically valid under a diffuse spectrum, whereas a covariance spike can produce a nonvanishing approximation error. Simulation studies examine empirical size and power under normal and nonnormal sampling. Averaging the trace estimates over fixed partitions improves their stability, but does not remove size inflation in the strongly correlated settings.

title: When Language Models Misinterpret Uncertainty in Earth System Mechanism Attribution
authors: Pouria Behnoudfar, Nan Chen
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30501v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mechanistic attribution in Earth system science requires quantifying uncertainty and communicating its implications. Here, we develop an uncertainty-aware mechanistic attribution pipeline that constructs probabilistic fingerprints from ensemble estimates, including covariance-aware separation of competing mechanisms, and an evidence ladder that systematically varies the information provided to language models (LLMs). We evaluate this framework in an idealized stochastic system and a coupled El Ni\~no model using controlled interventions and ensemble data assimilation. In the idealized system, numerical separation increases GPT-4o's intervention-label agreement from 0.80 to 0.98, but not GPT-4o-mini's. In the coupled system, both LLMs identify seven of eight fingerprint-ambiguous events when given full fingerprints with verbal interpretations; GPT-4o's false ambiguity reports decrease from 10/82 to 1/82, without consistent gains in intervention-label agreement. For eight historical ENSO events, the uncertainty-aware condition agrees with the model-inferred mechanism labels in seven cases. These findings distinguish uncertainty assessment from its communication.

title: Drinfeld presentation of affine iquantum groups via iHopf algebras
authors: Ming Lu, Xiaolong Pan
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30521v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Affine quantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf{U}}$ and affine iquantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ admit two complementary descriptions: a Serre-type presentation and a Drinfeld (current) presentation. While iquantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ are typically defined via the Serre presentation, their Drinfeld presentations are substantially more subtle and less well understood. In this paper, we give a conceptual derivation of the Drinfeld presentation of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ starting directly from the Drinfeld presentation of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}$, working within the framework of iHopf algebras. This approach leads naturally to the definition of iquantum affinization associated with arbitrary Kac-Moody algebras $\mathfrak{g}$. We further show that, in this general setting, these iquantum affinizations can be realized as coideal subalgebras of quantum affinizations with respect to the Drinfeld coproduct. Finally, in the affine case, we describe the imaginary root vectors $\Theta_{i,r}$ of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ explicitly in terms of the root vectors $\psi^\pm_{i,r}$ of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}$, thereby extending the results of Li and Prze\'zdziecki for certain affine types of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$.

title: The reverse Ritz inclusion: computable bounds on the pseudospectra of an operator by those of a finite-rank compression
authors: Isaia Nisoli
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30530v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider a bounded operator on a separable complex Hilbert space, reached only through its action on vectors and that of its adjoint, and split it along a subspace of finite dimension into a compression, a far block acting on the complement, and the two couplings between them. Given upper bounds on the norms of the couplings and of the far block, we show that outside a disc a pseudospectrum of the operator lies in a pseudospectrum of the compression, with an explicit loss in the level; this reverses the classical inclusion of the Ritz values in a pseudospectrum of the operator. The same bounds, with the smallest singular value of the shifted compression, bound the resolvent of the operator, count its eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity inside every contour outside the disc on which a computed inequality holds, and enclose its spectral projector; no normality, self-adjointness or positivity is used.

title: High-Order Fully Discrete Entropy-Stable DG Methods with Compact Explicit Single-Step Time Discretizations
authors: Yuchang Liu, Yan Jiang, Mengping Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30535v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a unified framework for high-order, fully discrete entropy-stable discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods with compact explicit single-step time discretizations. At the end of each time step, the preliminary DG polynomial is scaled toward its cell average to enforce a strong cell entropy inequality while preserving conservation. This correction is feasible if and only if the updated cell average satisfies a weak cell entropy inequality, which standard third-order strong-stability-preserving Runge--Kutta DG updates can violate at arbitrarily small positive CFL numbers. For compact single-step schemes, including compact Runge--Kutta, Lax--Wendroff, and ADER-DG methods, we derive an explicit interval of feasible numerical entropy fluxes at each interface and prove that it is nonempty under a CFL condition. Projecting a compatible high-order target flux onto this interval guarantees the weak cell entropy inequality and preserves single-step high-order accuracy on smooth solutions, including near nondegenerate extrema. The limiter also enforces multiple entropy inequalities simultaneously. We also establish a Lax--Wendroff-type theorem. Numerical experiments for scalar conservation laws and the compressible Euler equations demonstrate high-order accuracy, multi-entropy control, and robustness for strong shocks.

title: Matrix Triangle Inequalities: Past, Present, and Future
authors: Jean-Christophe Bourin, Teng Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30538v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This survey provides a concise overview of matrix triangle inequalities. Classical topics, such as inequalities for unitarily invariant norms, are revisited from a different perspective, with a particular emphasis on unitary orbit inequalities and various notions of matrix moduli. The exposition progresses from elementary results to much more recent developments, highlighting the evolution of the subject and its ongoing directions of research.

title: Very tight embeddings of subspaces of \(L_p\) for \(0<p<1\)
authors: Gang Cai, Longfa Sun
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For \(0

<1\) and \(\mu>1\), every \(d\)-dimensional subspace of \(L_p\) embeds linearly into \(\ell_p^{\lfloor\mu d\rfloor}\) with distortion at most \(C(p,\mu)(\log(d+2))^{1/p}\). If its Rademacher type \(q\) constant is at most \(T\), where \(p

title: Return Time Sets of Minimal Points for Countable Group Actions
authors: Jian Li, Yini Yang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30554v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For a countably infinite discrete group $G$, we study subsets of $G$ that contain a neighbourhood return-time set of a minimal point in a $G$-flow $X$. For $e\in F\subseteq G$, we characterize this property by the existence of $e\in A\subseteq F$ such that $\operatorname{Int}_K(A):=\{t\in G:Kt\subseteq A\}$ is right syndetic for every finite $K\subseteq A$, and equivalently by the support of a minimal binary configuration in the Bernoulli shift $2^G$. Additional conditions on $\operatorname{Int}_K(A) \operatorname{Int}_K(A)^{-1}$ characterize realization by minimal flows that are weakly mixing of all finite orders or strongly mixing: for every such $K$, the former requires that for each finite $H\subseteq G$ there is $c\in G$ with $HcH\subseteq \operatorname{Int}_K(A) \operatorname{Int}_K(A) ^{-1}$, whereas the latter requires that $\operatorname{Int}_K(A)\operatorname{Int}_K(A)^{-1}$ be cofinite. We also construct, for every compact metrizable minimal $G$-flow, a free minimal, strongly mixing Cantor flow disjoint from it.

title: Classification of binary, ternary and quaternary Hermitian LCD codes
authors: Keita Ishizuka
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30561v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We extend the complete classifications of linear complementary dual (LCD) codes from length 15 to length 19 in the binary case, from length 10 to length 15 in the ternary case and from length 12 to length 13 in the quaternary Hermitian case. The classification rests on a reduction of the monomial equivalence of LCD codes to graph isomorphism on the coordinates, combined with canonical augmentation.

title: Collinear motions in constant curvature spaces, and coplanar motions in $\mathbb{R^4}$
authors: Carlos Barrera-Anzaldo, Abimael Bengochea, Connor Jackman, Ernesto P\'erez-Chavela
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30567v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A collinear motion of an $n$-body problem is one in which the $n$-bodies always lie along some, possibly moving, geodesic during their evolution.
  We prove that every collinear motion of $n\geq 3$ bodies in a constant non-zero curvature space is necessarily contained in some fixed constant curvature space of dimension at most three. For natural systems admitting energy and angular momentum integrals, we further show that every such motion is necessarily a relative equilibrium: evolving under uniform rotation while maintaining constant mutual distances.
  These results extend certain classical results on collinear motions in Euclidean spaces, initiated by P. Pizzetti, to general spaces of constant curvature. The same methods also yield a partial answer to a question of A. Wintner. Namely, we show that any concave and always coplanar motion in the Euclidean 4-body problem, where the moving plane containing the bodies sweeps out an $\mathbb{R}^4$, must be self-similar: maintaining constant mutual distance ratios over the motion.

title: Soft-Update MSA for Nonconvex Stochastic Optimal Control: Theory and Algorithms
authors: Shaolin Ji, Xinmeng Liu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.30585v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For the method of successive approximations (MSA), a fundamental challenge is that the stochastic maximum principle (SMP) provides an optimality condition rather than a descent rule. To overcome this difficulty for nonconvex stochastic control problems, we develop a soft-update MSA (SU-MSA) with a second-order-adjoint correction of the Hamiltonian and a neural realization called DeepSMP. Both an explicit stepsize rule guaranteeing cost descent and the convergence of the algorithm are established. Moreover, the global SMP condition is asymptotically satisfied when the corrected Hamiltonian is convex, while in a special case the cost is further proved to converge to the global optimum. To extend SU-MSA to high dimensions, we develop DeepSMP using a differentiable smooth approximation of the corrected Hamiltonian and analyze the convergence of the resulting objective and its gradient. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
